newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Sept 20.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Sept 20.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning.

** U.S. firm Amoco Corp has decided to scrap a proposed 40 billion cubic meter coalbed methane project in India costing $1 billion due to slow negotiations, spokesman Jim Spangler said on Thursday, adding that the company was now looking at projects in Poland and China
** The state-owned Bank of Baroda decides to cut its prime lending rate to 15.5 percent from 16 percent effective October 1 -- following the lead taken by State Bank of India to reduce lending rates
** Population growth and problems with water management in Asia should drive up demand for grains steadily in coming decades, Worldwatch Institute's director Lester Brown said on Thursday
** India is likely to become the world's largest importer of palm oil beating China, a Malaysian trade official says
** London silver prices sunk lower on Thursday and flirted with the psychological $5.00 an ounce level, dragging down the rest of the precious metals. Gold was off $0.50 lower at $382.85 an ounce
** The spot dollar/rupee INR= opened unchanged at 35.71/73 per dollar and seen quiet, dealers say
** On Thursday, shares across India drifted lower with sellers offloading stocks in the absence of any clear direction, brokers said.
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 64.24 points, or 1.88 percent, lower at 3,349.77 after rising to 3,430.83
** The 100-share National index fell 14.39 points, or 0.94 percent, at 1,509.10
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index dropped 16.0 points to 978
** The 500-share CRISIL index was off 7.91 points, or 1.19 percent, at 658.93.
** The Delhi share index slipped 18.07 points to 746.69
** The Calcutta index fell 7.77 points to 431.65
** The Madras index shed 5.95 points to 3,443.20
